analysis.title: From Panic to FOMO: Max Pain Market Continues
key_insights: NDX futures briefly dipped below a major trendline and are back above it. A large upside candle is forming today. The 200-day MA remains higher.
Nasdaq had its largest single-day market capitalization loss on record last Thursday.
GS data shows US fundamental L/S gross leverage had its largest weekly decline since Covid, falling to 207.5% (26th percentile over the past year). Net leverage is at five-year lows.
The momentum factor sold off sharply. After a move of this size, even a small bounce could be explosive.
GS's panic vol index reached 9.57 on Thursday and closed the week at 9.2. Readings above 9 have historically offered good buying opportunities.

GS's new Multiple Surprise Ratio (MSR) compares a daily move to the previous day's one-month implied vol. SPX had its largest vol-adjusted surprise in 19 years last week, NDX ranked in the top two and the Russell 2000 in the top five, so options underestimated the moves.
Tech volatility remains elevated in absolute and relative terms despite today's bounce.

GS says CTA signals are negative in about 60% of global equity markets, including the S&P 500. Baseline flows are $28bn of SPX futures selling over the next week and $45bn over the next month, which could push CTA positioning net short.
risk_factors: CTA selling of $28bn over the next week and $45bn over the next month could push positioning net short.

The momentum factor has fallen sharply, so a bounce could be explosive in either direction.
